properties.statement:
A DESIGN CAN RECORD THAT SOMETHING VIOLATES A CONSTRAINT, A DESIGNRULE OR A REQUIREMENT, AND NO DETECTOR WILL EVER MENTION IT. Raised indirectly by the US-government genesis session, 2026-08-15 (docs/feedback/2026-08-15-usgov-genesis-session.md, item 3): 'reflow2 already has a VIOLATES edge type and does not appear to use it for this.' Measured here the same day, and the honest result is NARROWER THAN A FIRST PASS SUGGESTED — recorded with the correction because the overstatement is the kind this project keeps catching.

WHAT IS TRUE: `grep VIOLATES` over `crates/reflow2-core/src/detect.rs` returns NOTHING. No gap type is computed from the edge. Nothing asks 'does anything violate this?'.

WHAT IS NOT TRUE, and was claimed before checking properly: that the edge is read by nothing at all. It is named at `crates/reflow2-core/src/propagate.rs:34` in `RISK_EDGES` (`RISKS, BLOCKS, CONTRADICTS, VIOLATES, MASKS`), so `propagate_change` counts it as a risk crossing, and reflow2's own design holds 4 instances. A case-sensitive search for the Rust-style `Violates` finds nothing while the string constant `VIOLATES` is used — which is how the wrong conclusion was reached. NOTE that this also places it OUTSIDE the eight declared-and-unreached edges measured in `dec:idea-detect-vocabulary-that-nothing-reaches`: by that node's own three-part test VIOLATES is REACHED, and it is right about that.

SO THE DEFECT IS THE ASYMMETRY, NOT DEADNESS: the edge is storable, propagatable, and undetectable. Every other traceability claim in the design gets a detector that asks whether it is missing — an unsatisfied Requirement, an unallocated Capability, an unrealized Capability, an unverified claim. A VIOLATION is the one claim the design can hold that no report will surface, so it is visible only to somebody who already went looking at the node it hangs off.

WHY IT MATTERS AND WHERE IT CAME FROM: the governance session's suggestion (c) was that a prohibition is checkable against a design — 'you look for something that VIOLATES it'. That is exactly right, and once prohibitions are modelled as Constraints (see `fact:defect-the-constraint-vocabulary-is-documented-as-numeric-so-the-right-node-is-ruled-out`, which shows they should be) the noise problem that prompted the suggestion disappears on its own, because `unsatisfied_requirement` stops firing on them. WHAT REMAINS IS THE BETTER HALF: a positive check. A design that has recorded a violation should say so, once, where people already look.

WHAT IS ESTABLISHED: no detector reads the edge; propagate does; 4 instances exist here. WHAT IS NOT: whether a violation detector should fire as a gap (a recorded violation may be a KNOWN and accepted tension rather than a fault — this design uses CONTRADICTS with `alignment` for exactly that nuance and VIOLATES has no such property), and whether severity would need to come from somewhere.
